subject: Secure deployment discovery — network & residency constraints (next steps)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lars Jensen <lars.jensen@curahealth.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@curahealth.com>
Date: 2029-05-04T14:10:00Z
Subject: Secure deployment discovery — network & residency constraints (post-call recap)

Lars / Elena — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete asks we discussed so we stay aligned.

Key business driver
- CuraHealth needs an air-gapped / private deployment option for processing patient PII and diagnostic outputs to meet EU data residency and local regulator expectations.

Primary technical constraints you flagged
- No inbound connections to on-prem environment allowed; only outbound TLS to a whitelist of Redwood egress endpoints via an outbound proxy.
- Egress is strictly controlled; traffic must flow through your perimeter proxy and be restricted by FQDN/IP; no wildcard egress.
- KV cache persistence must be encrypted using customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) with no plaintext token retention.
- Storage residency: logs and model artifacts must remain in EU region; audit logs need 2-year retention with access controls.
- Operational requirement: ability to run an offline “airgap” install for pre-production testing inside a sealed lab.

Summary of what Redwood can provide (high-level)
- Private (VPC) deployment with customer-managed network controls, support for outbound-only routing through proxy, and optional on-prem appliance for fully air-gapped installs.
- KMS integrations and audit logging hooks; we can support HSM-backed keys via your vendor (Yubico/Thales) in the common patterns.
- A staged rollout: internal staging (limited dataset), followed by canary on a subset of jobs, then full production cutover.

Action items we agreed on (owners & ETA)
1) CuraHealth: share your network egress whitelist and proxy FQDNs (Lars) — ETA: 2029-05-08
2) CuraHealth: export of minimal sample dataset and classification of PII elements for data flow review (Elena) — ETA: 2029-05-10
3) Redwood: draft technical checklist for airgap install and required artifacts (Mina) — ETA: 2029-05-06 (attached)
4) Redwood: internal alignment call with engineering to confirm KMS/HSM patterns and any custom connector work (Ben & Jordan) — schedule by 2029-05-07

Attachments: redwood-deployment-checklist.pdf (checklist), network-ports-matrix.xlsx (template for egress mapping).

If any of the items above are incorrect or missing, flag them and I’ll update. Proposed next step: 60-minute technical deep-dive on Mon 2029-05-13 with your network & security leads so we can confirm port/FQDN lists and validate the airgap procedures.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad

From: Lars Jensen <lars.jensen@curahealth.com>

Date: 2029-05-04T18:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Secure deployment discovery — network & residency constraints (post-call recap)

Thanks Mina — helpful summary and yes, we’re aligned on the high-level. A couple of clarifications from our side after reviewing your checklist: 

- Outbound proxy: we do not allow direct TLS egress to arbitrary IPs. Everything must be proxied through our BlueGate proxy which does TLS termination and SNI inspection. We can provide the proxy FQDNs and the upstream allowlist (IP ranges) but those are updated nightly.
- For the airgap appliance: the lab install will be completely isolated with intermittent manual media transfer (sneakernet) for the initial model artifact sync. We’ll need a documented procedure for offline package validation and integrity checks (hashes + signing).
- KMS/HSM: we use Thales Luna; we cannot export keys. Any integration must call the HSM via our internal network.

We’ll upload the egress FQDN list and a sanitized sample dataset to the secure share by 2029-05-08.

Lars
IT Security Lead — CuraHealth

Subject: Re: Secure deployment discovery — network & residency constraints (post-call recap)

Appreciate the clarifications, Lars — that helps. A few follow-ups from our engineering/readiness side: 

1) Offline package strategy: Jordan, can your team outline the signing + integrity check flow we’d provide for an airgap install? If we produce signed tarballs with SHA-512 and a detached signature we can support manual validation in-lab.
2) HSM integration: Ben, I’ve noted CuraHealth uses Thales Luna and that keys cannot be exported. We’ll need to confirm whether we can call the HSM over a peered internal network or if the HSM calls must be proxied through an internal gateway.
3) Network testing: once we receive the proxy FQDNs and allowlist, we’ll provide a short test harness for connectivity checks (TLS handshake, SNI, and endpoint certificate validation).

Ben / Jordan — can we lock a 45-minute internal alignment call tomorrow (2029-05-06) to confirm the engineering tasks and estimate level-of-effort? I’m including the deployment checklist and the egress template we discussed.

Best,

Mina
